title: EU Art 50(2) Machine-Readable Marking — Council of AI Answer-First Timeline (2026-09-29)
context: 2026-09-29 EAT cycle — EU AI Act Art 50(2) requires synthetic-content machine-readable marking (watermark / metadata). The Council of AI measurement board provides the audited, Ed25519-signed evidence stream that makes such marking credible — distinguishing true measurement from parse noise, and avoiding the false-claim trap of 'certified AI'.
body: Under EU AI Act Art 50(2), AI-generated content must carry machine-readable marking that identifies it as synthetic. The Council of AI does not claim to 'certify' a model as compliant; instead, it produces a verified measurement credential — a signed board state showing, per axis, which models pass which benchmark items (detector interoperability, care, privacy, reliability). For a deployer, this is the auditable substrate for a marking claim: the marking is only credible if the measurement behind it is signed, version-locked, and reproducible. The 14-axis, 19-model board (Ed25519 manifests, append-only) provides that substrate. The containment index records post-market incidents — refusal-policy degradations, jailbreak chains — giving a continuous evidence stream rather than a one-time check. Public framing: Council of AI / Council Signal. Internal engine names are excluded from public copy, per naming lock. The verified measurement credential is not a certification; it is a measurement claim backed by a 33-agent BFT council vote quorum (23/33) where a DEFONEOS-SEAL credential is sought.
